Same body, two measurements — a mismatch between those two numbers is NOT drift and must never be read as one. PREVIOUS NOTE: STAGED, NOT APPLIED — Security review REQUIRED (it patches hr_apply). F3 from the 2026-09-13 review: a `buff_apply` for item X is REFUSED `buff_not_paid` unless the SAME delta carries `items[X] = -1`. The debit IS the possession check and it lives at the layer that holds the lock: the items block already refuses an unknown id, clamps the magnitude, takes `for update` on the inventory row and refuses `insufficient_item` when the stack cannot cover it, so this file adds a COUPLING and no inventory logic of its own. EXACTLY -1 (a buff is one serving; -2 would mean either a second buff the merge never saw or a double debit, and "eat three at once" is a design change). Ordered AFTER the catalogue lookup so an unknown or non-buff item still answers the more specific `bad_buff_item`, and BEFORE the server clock is read so a refusal never reaches the merge. `buff_not_paid` is a release code (nothing was written; the honest client response is "send the debit too", which is the same intent with the same key). Without it the possession check would live in the Edge Function — the layer that PROPOSES, not the one holding the lock — and a stale or compromised engine could buff a character who has never cooked the food. Nothing exploits it today (step 2's eat path is the only emitter and is not wired), which is why it is a follow-up and not a hotfix. TWO anchored splices on hr_apply (release codes, validation block), both on text THIS LANE authored one migration ago — the one part of that 26-patch body an agent can account for line by line — each asserted EXACTLY ONCE in §0, re-entrant, RESTATEMENT-DEBT-ACK in the header. §0 also refuses to install unless the buff_apply block AND an items block that refuses insufficient_item are both present, so it cannot become a coupling to nothing. §2 EXECUTES inside an HR826-rolled-back subtransaction: a bare buff_apply is refused buff_not_paid with the queue and the bag unmoved; items[X] = 0, -2, +1, +5 and a DIFFERENT item's debit are all refused; the paid form applies and spends exactly one; a character holding none is refused insufficient_item by the items block that owns the lock; no predecessor block was eaten; no client role can execute hr_apply. Net-zero leak check over 5 tables. No table, column, index, ledger row or grant change — two jsonb lookups on a delta already in memory, at most once per apply.
